strategy.rationale: Separates the investigation into three distinct, non-overlapping empirical domains: rigorous benchmark metrics, open-source ecosystem/scaffolding activity, and real-world developer discussions to assess the 2026 feasibility of open-weight coding models replacing paid agents.

dimensions.name: Research Benchmarks & Coding Capability Evaluation
dimensions.description: Evaluate and compare state-of-the-art open-weight models against leading proprietary coding agents on standard software engineering benchmarks.
key_questions: How do leading open-weight models (DeepSeek-Coder-V2/V3, Qwen 2.5 Coder, Llama 3.1/3.3, Codestral) compare against frontier commercial models (Claude 3.5/3.7 Sonnet, GPT-4o, OpenAI o1/o3-mini) on SWE-bench Verified, SWE-bench Lite, LiveCodeBench, and Aider LLM leaderboard?
What are the key architectural and capability gaps between open-weight models and proprietary models in agentic code generation, multi-file editing, tool use, and long-context repository reasoning?
What trajectory do research benchmark curves demonstrate heading into 2026 for open-weight coding models?
dimensions.focus: SWE-bench Verified/Lite scores, LiveCodeBench, HumanEval/MBPP, Aider benchmarks, agentic tool execution accuracy, and benchmark trendlines.

sources.description: SWE-bench, LiveCodeBench, and model technical report preprints and benchmark papers
Benchmark leaderboards, Anthropic/OpenAI/DeepSeek/Qwen official benchmark releases and technical reports
Aider LLM benchmark leaderboard, LMSYS Chatbot Arena Coding Leaderboard, and independent evaluation suites

dimensions.time_sensitivity: High time sensitivity; focus on late 2024 through 2026 state-of-the-art benchmarks and model releases

owns: Quantitative coding benchmark scores (SWE-bench, LiveCodeBench, Aider, HumanEval)
Comparative accuracy, pass rates, and error analyses between proprietary and open-weight models on standardized tasks
Model capability trajectories and benchmark-level gap analyses
excludes: Ecosystem repository metrics and download statistics
Subjective developer testimonials and forum sentiments
shared_topics: Model family definitions (DeepSeek, Qwen, Llama, Claude, GPT)
scope_ownership.overlap_policy: d1 owns all standardized benchmark scores and formal capability measurements; d2 and d3 reference these model names but do not recalculate benchmark scores.

dimensions.name: Hugging Face, Open-Source Scaffolding & GitHub Ecosystem Activity
dimensions.description: Analyze Hugging Face download velocity, model quantization availability, and GitHub developer tooling ecosystems that turn raw open-weight models into autonomous coding agents.
key_questions: What do Hugging Face download volumes, community finetunes, and model releases indicate about open-weight coding adoption (DeepSeek, Qwen-2.5-Coder, Starcoder, Mistral)?
How mature are open-source agentic harnesses (Aider, OpenHands/OpenDevin, Cline/Roo-Code, Continue.dev) when powered by open-weight models via Ollama, vLLM, SGLang, or LiteLLM?

What are the hardware, inference speed, VRAM, and total cost of ownership (TCO) realities of running capable local coding agents vs paying subscription fees (e.g., $20/mo for Claude Pro/Cursor vs hardware investments)?
dimensions.focus: Hugging Face model statistics, GitHub stars/commits/releases for agent harnesses, local inference engines, and VRAM/hardware feasibility.

sources.description: GitHub repositories for Aider, OpenHands, Cline, Continue, Ollama, vLLM, and SGLang
Hugging Face model hub cards, model download metrics, and quantization ecosystem releases
Documentation and hardware specifications from open-source inference frameworks and hardware guides

dimensions.time_sensitivity: Focus on 2024-2026 ecosystem developments, tooling updates, and modern quantization methods

owns: Hugging Face download trends, model availability, and quantization (GGUF, AWQ, EXL2)
GitHub ecosystem activity for open-source agent frameworks (Aider, OpenHands, Cline, Continue)
Hardware requirements (VRAM, GPU compute), local inference economics, and infrastructure TCO
excludes: Unstructured forum discussions on HN and Stack Overflow
shared_topics: Agent tool calling and workflow definitions
scope_ownership.overlap_policy: d2 owns the tooling, infrastructure, downloads, and execution frameworks; d1 handles benchmark scores and d3 handles developer qualitative sentiment.

dimensions.name: Developer Sentiment & Real-World Pragmatics on Hacker News & Stack Overflow
dimensions.description: Gather practitioner experiences, qualitative feedback, community debates, and real-world enterprise adoption hurdles regarding open-weight models vs paid coding assistants.
key_questions: What is the prevailing developer consensus on Hacker News and Stack Overflow regarding the daily usability of local/open-weight models vs Claude 3.5/3.7 Sonnet or Cursor?
What real-world pain points (hallucination in complex codebases, context window degradation, multi-file coherence, latency, setup friction) do developers report when trying to replace paid tools?
What enterprise considerations (data privacy, IP compliance, offline security vs developer productivity) drive teams toward or away from open-weight coding agents in 2026?
dimensions.focus: Qualitative developer threads, practical failure modes, workflow friction, privacy/IP motivations, and consensus regarding realistic replacement in 2026.

sources.description: Hacker News discussions, Ask HN threads, and community post-mortems
Stack Overflow discussions, developer surveys, Reddit r/LocalLLaMA and r/programming practitioner threads
Engineering blog posts, team case studies, and practitioner experience reports

dimensions.time_sensitivity: Active community sentiment and practitioner retrospectives from 2024 through 2026

owns: Hacker News, Stack Overflow, and developer forum discussions and sentiment analysis
Real-world workflow friction, multi-file editing failure modes, and user experience tradeoffs
Enterprise privacy, IP governance, and compliance drivers vs SaaS productivity
excludes: GitHub repository code analysis and raw download metrics
shared_topics: Commercial tool definitions (Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Devin, Claude Code)
scope_ownership.overlap_policy: d3 owns qualitative developer feedback, real-world case studies, and enterprise sentiment; references facts from d1 and d2 without duplicating their primary data collection.

notes: Plan designed to rigorously investigate the technological, operational, and economic feasibility of open-weight coding agents replacing commercial equivalents in 2026.
